theory.intro: 12-hour time uses am and pm; 24-hour time uses four digits from $0000$ to $2359$. We can swap between them with a simple rule.
facts: **am** times, except those in the $12$ am hour, keep the same hour: $7\!:\!30$ am $= 0730$ (write a leading zero for hours under $10$). The entire $12$ am hour becomes hour $00$.
**pm** times, except those in the $12$ pm hour, add $12$ to the hour: $3\!:\!15$ pm $= 1515$. The entire $12$ pm hour keeps hour $12$.
steps: For am: hours $1$–$11$ keep the hour; add a leading zero if needed. The entire $12$ am hour becomes hour $00$. Keep the minutes unchanged.
For pm: hours $1$–$11$ add $12$ to the hour. The entire $12$ pm hour stays hour $12$. Keep the minutes unchanged.
To go back: hour $00$ is $12$ am; hours $01$–$11$ keep the hour and use am; hour $12$ stays $12$ and uses pm; hours $13$–$23$ are pm (subtract $12$). Keep the minutes unchanged.

foundation.solution_text:
The time is am, so keep hour $6$ and add a leading zero.
$6{:}25\text{ am}=0625$

The time is am, so keep hour $11$.
$11{:}40\text{ am}=1140$

$08$ is before $12$, so the time is am.
$0830=8{:}30\text{ am}$

development.solution_text:
Midnight begins a new day at hour $00$.
$12{:}00\text{ am}=0000$

Noon-hour pm times keep hour $12$.
$12{:}35\text{ pm}=1235$

mastery.solution_text:
